national_raw_news.content: The 80th Independence Day celebrations this year will highlight Yuva Shakti and the contribution of young India towards building a Viksit Bharat by 2047, along with the commemoration of 150 years of the National Song, Vande Mataram. Briefing media in New Delhi today, Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh said, the celebrations will be led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi from the historic Red Fort. The Prime Minister will unfurl the National Flag and address the nation. A major highlight of this year’s celebrations will be the commemoration of 150 years of Vande Mataram. For the first time, the National Song will be sung from the ramparts of the Red Fort during the Independence Day ceremony. The ramparts will be decorated with floral arrangements based on the theme of Vande Mataram, while around 2 thousand 5 hundred NCC cadets and My Bharat volunteers will form a ‘Vande Mataram’ formation on Gyanpath. Vande Mataram will also be sung collectively at the Red Fort with Service bands, with everyone present standing at attention. Following the Prime Minister’s address, NCC cadets and My Bharat volunteers will sing the National Song, followed by the National Anthem. Mi-17 helicopters will participate in the ceremony, with the aerial display featuring the National Flag, flower petals and a special banner commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram. As part of the nationwide celebrations, armed forces and other uniformed service bands will perform at 343 prominent locations from 8th to 15th of this month. Bands of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Coast Guard, NCC, CRPF, ITBP, CISF, SSB, BSF, IDS, RPF and Assam Rifles will participate. The second major theme of the celebration is ‘Yuva Shakti – Leading the Journey to Viksit Bharat@2047’. Nineteen medal-winning students from the 2026 International Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Mathematics Olympiads have been invited as special guests, along with young innovators, PM Internship Scheme interns, startups, PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana trainees, My Bharat volunteers and beneficiaries of various government schemes. Around 5 hundred Delhi government school students, selected through quizzes and competitions, will also attend the ceremony. The celebrations will also recognize other contributors to the Viksit Bharat vision, including women entrepreneurs supported under PM Mudra, PMAY-U beneficiaries, innovators and scientists, Bharat Taxi Sarthis, PM Surya Ghar beneficiaries, PM Vishwakarma artisans, PM Shram Yogi Maandhan beneficiaries, farmers and International Yoga Day volunteers. More than 15 hundred Delhi-based people representing different States and Union Territories and dressed in traditional attire have been invited. For invitees, Delhi Metro services will begin at 4 AM and will be free of cost. Around 2 hundred My Bharat and NCC volunteers will assist visitors, including those requiring wheelchair assistance. Cloakrooms, drinking water, toilets and rain ponchos will also be available, while parking locations will be provided through Google Maps and Mappls. After the ceremony, NCC cadets and My Bharat volunteers will undertake a Swachhata campaign at the Red Fort, focusing on systematic plogging and prompt removal of garbage.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 165 Parliament passes Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill to recognise digital banking records as lega...
national_raw_news.content: Parliament has passed the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026, with the Rajya Sabha approving it today. Lok Sabha has already passed the Bill. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman moved the Bill, which aims to modernise the legal framework to meet the requirements of the present banking system. The Bill seeks to provide a law relating to evidence with respect to bankers’ books and to align it with contemporary digital banking practices. The Bill also has a provision that an electronic or digital record of a banker’s book will be admissible, valid, and legally enforceable as evidence. Replying to discussion on the bill, Finance Minister Sitharaman said that this bill is a very reformative step, which will help the country move forward at a faster pace. She highlighted that the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act was framed in 1891, when banking systems were entirely paper-based. Mrs Sitharaman said, today, India has demonstrated remarkable progress in digitising its economy. She said, banking and financial transactions are now largely driven by digital platforms, often accessible through a simple click on a mobile phone. The Minister said that in such a scenario, it is imperative that the country’s legal framework evolves to keep pace with these advancements. She noted that the existing 1891 Act relies heavily on certified copies of physical bank records as admissible evidence in legal proceedings. Mr Sitharaman said that the Bill establishes a technology-neutral legal framework for bankers’ records, which formally recognises electronic and digital banking records and ensures their admissibility in legal proceedings. It also standardises the certification process and allows authentication through manual, digital, and electronic signatures. Earlier, participating in the discussion, Arun Singh of BJP said that new legislation has been brought to change old act framed in 1891 under British rule. Mr Singh said, this bill will further boost the banking system, which is considered as the backbone of the Indian economy. He said, a revolutionary transformation is being witnessed in the banking system under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr Singh said, the bill has the provision that evidences in the digital or computerised form will be accepted as part of evidence. Manas Ranjan Mangaraj of BJD supported the objectives of the bill. He said, data security and privacy must be given the highest priority. He said, as the banking records contain sensitive personal and financial information, the government must ensure strong safeguards to prevent misuse, unauthorized access and cyber threats. Other members also spoke on the bill

national_raw_news.title: 4 hours ago | National 213 LS passes Tribunals Reforms Bill, aims to improve transparency & efficiency of Tribunals
national_raw_news.content: Lok Sabha has passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026. The Bill was passed without discussion amidst opposition uproar. As the pandemonium continued, the Chair adjourned the House for the day to meet again at 11:00 AM tomorrow. Earlier, when the House reassembled after the second adjournment at 2:00 PM, Minister of State for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal moved the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, amid the opposition uproar. The bill aims to improve efficiency, ensure independence, transparency, and uniformity in the qualifications, appointment of service of Chairpersons and Members of various Tribunals, as well as the administration and functioning of the Tribunals. The legislation also proposes to establish a National Tribunals Commission. Mr Meghwal said that the Bill has been brought as part of the reform express being rolled out across various sectors under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said, the purpose of tribunals is not to replace courts but to function as complementary institutions in modern governance. They deal with specialized matters such as taxation, company law, environment, securities market, intellectual property, and other regulatory domains, with the objective of ensuring speedy and effective delivery of justice. Mr Meghwal highlighted that under the leadership of Mr Modi, the government initiated the process of rationalisation of tribunals in 2015. The Minister said that the Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026 has been brought to establish a modern, independent, and uniform tribunal ecosystem. Mr Meghwal highlighted that the bill is aimed at strengthening governance, appointments, institutional independence, transparency, and efficiency. He said, the National Tribunals Commission will be established and it will be chaired by a former Judge of the Supreme Court or a former Chief Justice of a High Court. . The Presiding Officer, Jagdambika Pal repeatedly requested the protesting members to back to their seat and allow the House to function. He said that the entire nation is watching that who is responsible for the disruption of the House. Mr Pal said, the House is meant for discussion, but since the very first day of the Monsoon Session, the opposition members are continuously causing disruptions. Mr Pal said that Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju has already accepted their demand that Union Home Minister Amit Shah is ready to give a statement on the issue related to the student protest.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 111 Union Minister Kiren Rijiju appeals to opposition to allow HM Amit Shah to make statement
national_raw_news.content: Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju today said that the Government is ready for a detailed discussion in Parliament regarding the recent student protests and related issues. Assuring that Home Minister Amit Shah is ready to respond to every point, Mr Rijiju stated that citizens have a right to know the facts. He urged the Opposition to maintain order on the floor and refrain from further obstructing proceedings. Speaking to reporters at the Parliament premises after the Business Advisory Committee (BAC) meeting, Mr Rijiju appealed to the Opposition to allow the House to function so that Home Minister Amit Shah makes a statement about the students’ protest and addresses all concerns raised by the opposition members. The Minister emphasized that the Government has never shied away from parliamentary debates. He highlighted that during the BAC meeting, the government clearly communicated its willingness to hold a comprehensive discussion on the matter.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 176 India scripted successful conservation journey from 523 lions to 891 in last 10 years: PM Modi on...
national_raw_news.content: On the occasion of World Lion Day, Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said that India’s Asiatic lion population is thriving, with its habitat and range expanding. Sharing an article written by Union Minister Bhupender Yadav, Mr Modi highlighted that the Government’s unwavering commitment to conservation, backed by strong community participation, is an inspiring example of protecting the country’s wildlife and preserving the species for generations to come. The article written by Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupendra Yadav points out that the lions’ range has expanded from around 30 thousand square kilometres in 2020 to nearly 35 thousand square kilometres, covering 11 districts. It also talks about how India scripted the successful conservation journey of 523 lions in 2015 to 891 in 2025.

national_raw_news.title: Dr. Jitendra Singh calls For Enhancing Private Sector Participation In India’s Biotech Ecosystem
national_raw_news.content: Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has called for enhancing private sector participation in India’s Biotechnology ecosystem to strengthen industry outreach to promote indigenous products and technologies in biotechnology and life sciences. The Minister said this during a meeting with senior officials of the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) in New Delhi. During the meeting, Dr Singh stressed the need to build stronger linkages between India’s indigenous biotechnology capabilities, industry and investors such that innovations can move from research and development to commercialisation at a faster pace. The meeting focused on the implementation of the BIRAC Research, Development and Innovation Fund, integrating Life Sciences Global Capability Centres with the domestic biotech ecosystem, leveraging Corporate Social Responsibility for biotechnology-led initiatives. It also aimed to enhance BIRAC’s outreach and international visibility, and create stronger investor linkages for biotechnology startups and enterprises.

national_raw_news.title: Indonesia: Efforts intensify to combat wildfires spread over more than 107,000 hectares
national_raw_news.content: Indonesia intensified efforts to combat wildfires that have burned more than 107,000 hectares, deploying hundreds of firefighters and helicopters as blazes spread across the country during an unusually dry season. The largest fire is burning in Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java, where about 743 hectares have been scorched. Authorities closed the popular tourist destination, including areas around Mount Bromo, until further notice. No injuries or evacuations have been reported. Indonesia’s Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs Djamari Chaniago said cloud-seeding operations were unlikely to be possible through 18th of August because there were no suitable rain-bearing clouds. Firefighters are instead relying on water bombing and ground crews.

national_raw_news.title: Strait of Hormuz not to be reopened till US naval blockage continues: Iran’s FM spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei
national_raw_news.content: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said today that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the US continues its naval blockade against Iran. Addressing a weekly press briefing in Tehran, Baqaei said that the Strait of Hormuz was closed due to the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran. He emphasised that the reopening of the waterway relies on the conditions enforced on Iran and the Strait of Hormuz by the US and Israeli authorities. Baqaei mentioned that the talks between Iran and Oman over a shipping route is a bilateral matter which involves two nations. Earlier, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Aragchi stated that there are currently no ongoing negotiations with the United States.

national_raw_news.title: Over ten lakh people evacuated as typhoon Dolphin batters parts of Eastern China
national_raw_news.content: Chinese authorities have evacuated more than one million people from eastern China, including Shanghai, as Typhoon Dolphin made landfall. The typhoon brought heavy rain and disrupted transport across the region. Nearly 1,000 flights were cancelled in Shanghai today. Authorities have downgraded Dolphin to a tropical storm. China had earlier issued its highest-level red alert for Dolphin, which is the strongest storm to hit the country this year. Dolphin had maximum wind speeds of 150 kilometres per hour when it first struck Yuhuan in Zhejiang province yesterday. Heavy rain has been forecast for Shandong, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu and Zhejiang provinces. Shanghai is also expected to receive heavy rainfall. Authorities have urged people to avoid outdoor activities. Several major tourist attractions remain closed. These include parts of Disneyland and Legoland, as well as several viewing platforms along Shanghai’s Bund. national_raw_news.title: Hockey World Cup to be played in new format; quarterfinal stage scrapped 1 hour ago 31
national_raw_news.content: The FIH Hockey Men’s and Women’s World Cup 2026 will feature a revamped competition structure, with the traditional quarterfinal stage scrapped and the top two teams from each of the two crossover pools advancing directly to the semi-finals. Belgium and the Netherlands jointly host the tournament from August 15 to 30. The new format means teams will have little margin for error from the outset, with results from the opening pool stage potentially carrying over into the next phase. India’s men have been drawn alongside England, Pakistan and Wales in Pool D, while the Indian women will face China, England and South Africa in their Pool D campaign. The tournament will begin with the 16 teams in each competition split across four pools of four. From August 15 to 20, every team will play three matches against the other sides in its pool, with the final standings determining the composition of the next phase. The top two teams from Pools A and D will move into Pool E, while the leading two teams from Pools B and C will form Pool F. The top two finishers from Pool E and Pool F will advance directly to the last four. The women’s tournament will conclude in the Netherlands on August 29, with the bronze-medal match followed by the final. The men’s World Cup will conclude in Belgium a day later, on August 30, with its bronze-medal match and final.

national_raw_news.title: India secures two medals at World Athletics U20 Championships in US 6 hours ago 122
national_raw_news.content: In the World Athletics U20 Championships, India enjoyed a historic day in Eugene, USA, with Basant Kumar Meghwal and Shahnavaz Khan becoming the first Indians to win medals in the high jump and long jump at the championships. Basant Kumar Meghwal, the reigning Asian U20 champion, won silver in the men’s high jump with a personal best clearance of 2.21 metres. Shahnavaz Khan claimed bronze in the men’s long jump with a best effort of 7.84 metres. Algeria’s Younes Ayachi won the high jump gold, while Great Britain’s Otis Poole took bronze. The two medals took India’s tally at the championships to three. India have now equalled their medal haul from the 2021 and 2022 editions.

national_raw_news.title: Parliament passes Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill to enhance ease of doing business 53 mins ago 37
national_raw_news.content: Parliament has passed the Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill 2026 today with Rajya Sabha returning it to Lok Sabha after discussion. Lok Sabha has already passed the Bill. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman moved the bill. The Bill seeks to amend the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the Income-tax Act, 2025, and the Finance Act, 2026. The bill will replace the Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026, which was promulgated on 5th June this year. The Ordinance was promulgated with the objective of mitigating the impact of external economic shocks, ensuring stability in the domestic economy and supporting key sectors affected by the prevailing global conditions by amending certain provisions of the Act. The Bill further exempts foreign institutional investors and the Bank for International Settlements from paying income tax on interest earned on investments in government securities. The exemption will apply to income arising on or after 1st April this year. Previously, under the Income-tax Act, interest income was taxed at 20 per cent, short-term capital gains at 30 per cent and long-term capital gains at 12.5 per cent. The Bill further amends the Income-tax Act to exempt income earned by certain foreign companies from the sale of rough diamonds in a notified special zone. Replying to the discussion, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that the objective of the Bill is to strengthen India’s manufacturing ecosystem, attract further investment, generate employment, and promote manufacturing activities. She said the second major reform relates to providing tax exemptions to foreign companies procuring data services from specified data centres in India. Ms Sitharaman noted that the measure will enhance ease of doing business for global cloud service providers, expand India’s data centre ecosystem, and support the development of AI-driven data cities. She informed that these reforms will significantly benefit Indian companies as existing data centers will expand their operations. The Minister clarified that the Bill does not impose any tax or transaction charge on UPI users. Ms Sitharaman said that the electronic payment modes will continue to receive statutory protection against charges. The Minister said no Merchant Discount Rate, MDR framework has been finalized. She assured that small merchants and consumers will not have to pay MDR charges on UPI. The Finance Minister said this amendment is also aimed at attracting global diamond trading activities. It is also intended to promote a comprehensive ecosystem for financing, buying, and selling of diamonds within the country. Ms Sitharaman said that with the proposed tax exemptions, these global players can establish wholesale trading operations in India, making them more accessible to Indian buyers. She informed that the broader objective is to bring the entire value chain of the diamond trade to India. Earlier, participating in the discussion, Tarun Chugh of BJP supported the Bill saying it will support the progress of the nation, both locally as well as globally. He said that the Bill will give a significant boost to the nation’s economy and further strengthen the vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. P Wilson of...

national_raw_news.title: 1601 series to be used for transactional and service calls other than banks, Fin and govt entities: TRAI 2 hours ago 40
national_raw_news.content: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) today issued the Direction on use of 1601 series numbers for the transactional and service calls by the entities in sectors other than Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) sector, and Government entities which are using numbers from 1600 series. The Department of Communications informed TRAI has now initiated phase-wise implementation of the 1601-series allotted by the Department for similar calls by Utilities, Courier and Logistics sectors entities. This includes electricity distribution companies, water utilities, city gas distribution companies and LPG distribution entities. It also includes courier companies, express logistics companies, parcel delivery service providers, freight and logistics service providers engaged in delivery of consignments. This separate series has been issued in order to avoid mixing important financial voice calls with the service and transactional calls from the other sectors. The Ministry noted that the distinct numbering identity will enable the consumers to easily identify legitimate service and transactional calls, thereby strengthening trust in such voice-based communications. The 1601-series numbers will be allocated directly to eligible entities after due verification by the Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) and for this, TSPs have been asked to complete migration and onboarding of eligible entities within 90 days from the date of issue of the order.
